method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

proposedChanges.stem: A four-year-old needs venipuncture and wants a parent nearby. Which actions support coping? Select all that apply.
options: Use an agreed safe comfort position
Promise the needle will not hurt
Use detailed anatomical terminology to explain the procedure
why: Supportive positioning can improve security during the procedure.
An inaccurate promise may undermine trust.
A four-year-old needs simple concrete preparation matched to understanding, rather than technical anatomical detail.
A chosen suitable distraction can reduce procedural distress.

items.assessment: Restore privacy and involve a capable child in preferences; delaying coverage or bypassing the child for parental choice misses expressed embarrassment. CNO relationship/privacy reference replaces eating source.
Familiar settling routine targets the observed cause of sleep difficulty; ward-standard replacement may miss that cue. Pediatric sleep reference is now relevant.
Supporting the infant near the breast directly reduces the observed forward bending; chair adjustment alone may preserve the mismatch. Breastfeeding/postpartum refs replace general adult feeding.

Supported positioning away from painful incision preserves chosen feeding role. Shortened feeds or full substitution are unnecessary if adaptation is feasible; breastfeeding/postpartum refs match context.
Small frequent prescribed rehydration addresses vomiting with large drinks in an alert mildly ill child. Undiluted juice or long withholding is not the supplied plan; no rigid amount is invented.
Gentle care/barrier plus timely soiled-nappy change addresses irritant exposure. Thicker barrier cannot justify longer stool contact; diaper-rash reference now matches.

Assessing current barriers and supportive routine avoids treating temporary hospital accidents as deliberate behaviour. Pre-admission schedule may not fit current needs; toilet-learning reference is relevant.
Safe agreed adaptations balance cast limitations and adolescent privacy; avoid automatic dependence or full independence based on age. Hygiene and professional relationship refs support scope.

Gentle rinsing and prescribed comfort plan fit reassuring repaired-tear findings; fluid reduction, harsh antiseptic and fragrance may worsen irritation. Postpartum reference is relevant; worsening symptoms still require reassessment.
Side-lying directly addresses the observed supine late-pregnancy lightheadedness and is independently supported by NHS guidance; head/foot-only changes may not remove compression.

Persistent oral patches with feeding distress warrant assessment rather than assumed milk residue or repeated rubbing. Infant thrush reference now matches; item does not diagnose from description alone.
Observed sensory triggers support lower simultaneous stimulation and predictable care. Sensory-care reference is relevant to the accommodation; no diagnosis is inferred from behaviour.

Extra time/easier fastenings preserves participation during morning stiffness; repeated peak-stiffness practice or complete dressing substitution misses the timing/functional cue. Juvenile-arthritis source now relevant.
Accessible face-to-face communication addresses distance/lost cues before attributing wrong answers to cognition. Hearing-loss reference supports topic; infection precautions are not overridden.

Essential-needs/capacity assessment with sustainable support addresses missed care from exhaustion. Moving tasks without reviewing workload may relocate the burden. Caregiver-support reference now relevant.
Short safe prayer can be accommodated before assisted feeding; delaying ritual for staff schedule misses preference. Actual opened nutrition chapter explicitly supports this practice.
